scope: Hiwonder ROS Robot Control Board as used by this project; factory claims and project wiring are intentionally separate.

identity.official_revision_note: The current Hiwonder product page and documentation repository do not unambiguously publish a V1.2 hardware revision. The hardware-course FAQ explicitly discusses V1.0 and V1.1 only. Treat the project V1.2 label as physical/project evidence, not as an official online revision declaration.

official_sources.evidence: Current product specification identifies STM32F407VET6, two USB serial ports, four encoder-motor channels, mixed-voltage PWM servo ports, 7-14 V input, and onboard MPU6050.
Board diagram, schematic explanations, named MCU pins, power rails, motor/servo/USB/SBUS/CAN/I2C/display interfaces.
Factory example pin configurations, 1 Mbps host protocol examples, QMI8658 chapter, motor/encoder/SBUS/Bluetooth/display software paths.
Official documentation source repository used to avoid relying on rendered-page text alone.

board.source_note: Current product-page specifications describe the product family; they are not an independent physical inspection of this board.

input: DC 5 V to 12.6 V (hardware-course board diagram)
DC 7 V to 14 V (current product page)
power.source_conflict: The online sources disagree on the input range; do not use either range to approve a battery without checking the board marking and measured hardware.

encoder_motor.note: The eight driver pins are listed by the hardware schematic; the program chapter gives a concrete Motor 1 example.

pwm_servo.power_rails: 2 channels on VIN/battery voltage and 2 channels on 5 V
pwm_servo.factory_software_example: Four PWM servo objects are described; exact factory channel-to-pin mapping is not stated in the text source.

host_serial.recommended_factory_use: Serial port 2 for Raspberry Pi/Jetson communication; serial port 1 remains available for serial download/burning.

imu.conflict: The product page and hardware schematic call the device MPU6050, while program-analysis section 3.5 is titled QMI8658. The Hiwonder text does not provide a revision-specific, unambiguous WHO_AM_I value.

i2c_expansion.pullups: Hardware-course text says the I2C bus is pulled up on the onboard IMU.
i2c_expansion.sharing: The expansion connector and onboard IMU share the same I2C bus.

display.electrical: 3.3 V module in the program-analysis specification; the module pin description also mentions 3.3-5 V VCC.

sbus.format: 100000 baud, 9 data bits, even parity, 2 stop bits

usb_host.purpose: USB HID receivers such as game controllers

buzzer.conflict: The hardware-course schematic text says PA4; the program-analysis button chapter says PA8. Verify the board revision physically before treating either as universal.

can.termination: 120 ohm resistor stated by the hardware-course schematic explanation

interfaces.gpio_expansion: Reserved GPIO/SWD header; exact availability depends on the selected MCU peripherals and board routing.

protocol.checksum: low 8 bits of CRC over function, length, and data

host_link.not_factory_default: This deliberately differs from Hiwonder's documented USART3/PD8-PD9 factory example and serial-port-2 recommendation.

imu.interrupt_note: PB12 is configured as a normal input because PA12 owns shared EXTI12 for the HC-SR04 echo; the IMU integration polls I2C2.
imu.proof_path: host acceptance requires ready diagnostics, a valid sample, one of the two addresses, and WHO_AM_I 0x05

project_configured_motor_pwm.motor_4_missing_channel: PB9/TIM11 is not configured in the checked-in IOC/HAL post-init and is not commissioned

commissioned_scope.orientation_fusion: not published; raw SI acceleration and angular velocity are published
commissioned_scope.legacy_mpu_sources: retained for reference only and excluded from the production CMake target

verification_gates: Never infer the physical IMU from a stale MPU/QMI label; accept QMI only after WHO_AM_I 0x05 is read at 0x6A or 0x6B.
Never replace the project host UART with the factory USART3 mapping without an explicit physical wiring decision.
Treat official power, buzzer, IMU, and revision conflicts as unresolved until the board marking/schematic or measurement resolves them.
Any profile change must update the IOC/build/host contracts and this file in the same change.
